data.title: Boeing Makes List of Buys for the Modern-Day Industrial Revolution—Boeing Stock (NYSE:BA) Gains
data.description:
Have you ever considered what a modern-day industrial revolution might look like? Aerospace stock Boeing (BA) actually figures into it, based on a report from Barron's, that notes Boeing landed a slot in a list of buys for the modern-day industrial revolution. Investors found this news welcome enough, and gave Boeing a modest boost in Friday afternoon's trading. Boeing has seen a 10.9% loss in its share price over the past year.

It Has Nothing to Do With Steampunk

The Barron's report noted that Barclays analyst Anthony Valentini launched coverage of 20 different aerospace and defense stocks. Boeing, not surprisingly, made it onto that list with a Buy rating and a price target of $300 per share.

Defense stocks have been weak lately, mostly as investors start getting concerned about contract reform at the Pentagon and the midterm elections. If the midterm elections swing toward the Democrats, as some believe they might, then there could be some spending gridlock issues as the president looks for one thing to happen and Congress looks for completely different things. Boeing's positions in space travel, the defense industry, and commercial aircraft all make it a worthwhile pick as far as somebody who's looking for a modern-day industrial revolution is concerned.

Another New Buyer?

Meanwhile, Southwest Airlines (LUV) is apparently looking to buy Boeing 787s to start taking on long-haul international flights, according to a report from Live and Let's Fly. But that same report suggests that Southwest might actually be better off by using the planes it already has, but with a minor design change: adding lie-flat beds to the cabin spaces.

Naturally, Southwest hasn't made any decisions yet on this. But the report suggests that Southwest may be interested in a fleet of aircraft measuring in the dozens. Earlier reports suggest that Southwest may add anywhere from eight to 12 long-haul destinations in order to cover the bulk of locations that Southwest travelers want to go to. Whether or not Boeing will be a part of those plans is anybody's guess right now. But with many common European destinations running between 2,850 and 3,450 nautical miles, these should be well within reach for a 737 MAX 8, which has a range of around 3,550 nautical miles.

Is Boeing a Good Stock to Buy Right Now?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on BA stock based on 18 Buys and one Hold assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. The average BA price target of $273.13 per share implies 43.34% upside potential.

data.title: Strategy Stock (MSTR) Jumps 3% on Bullish Note from Barclays
data.description:
The stock of serial Bitcoin (BTC) acquirer Strategy (MSTR) is up 3% following a bullish note from British bank Barclays (BCS). In a note to client, analyst Nik Cremo raised his price target for MSTR stock to $175 from $160 previously. He also reiterated a Buy-equivalent overweight rating on Strategy's shares.

Cremo singled out Strategy as part of Braclays third-quarter earnings preview for the payments and financial technology sector. The analyst categorized Strategy and its stock alongside payment giants such as Visa (V) and Mastercard (MA). In his note, the analyst singled out Strategy for its resilience in weathering the "crypto winter" that took place from October 2025 until the end of this June.

Strategy's Fundamentals

Cremo also said that he likes the strong sector fundamentals and resilient consumer demand for the payments space heading into third-quarter earnings season. He attributed September's market volatility to interest rates increases and capital rotation into artificial intelligence (AI )stocks.

data.title: Aura Minerals Stock (AUGO) Soars Over 11% on a Q3 Mining Update
data.description:
Aura Minerals (AUGO) stock soared on Friday after the mining company provided investors with a business update. A press release from the company highlighted that it hit a new production record in the third quarter of 2026.

The gold miner produced 95,557 gold equivalent ounces (GEO), up 27% from the prior quarter and 29% from the same period last year. Sales reached 93,742 GEO, a 20% rise from the second quarter. For the first nine months of 2026, output totaled 253,131 GEO at current prices, up 28% year over year and the highest level for that period in the company's history.

Borborema and MSG led the gains. Borborema produced 22,842 GEO, a quarterly record and a 60% jump from the prior quarter. Higher ore grades and better plant feed drove the rise. At MSG, output climbed 85% to 13,321 GEO as work to restore the mine moved ahead. Aranzazu also had a strong quarter, with output up 39% from Q2 to 24,920 GEO.

Results varied across the other mines:

  • Apoena raised output 20% from the prior quarter to 6,865 GEO as work at its Nosde pit reached key high-grade areas.
  • Minosa output fell 7% to 13,344 GEO due to lower ore feed and the effects of a prior rise in leach-pad stacking levels.
  • Almas output dropped 12% to 14,264 GEO as lower grades offset gains from its plant upgrade. The company expects higher-grade ore to help Almas in the fourth quarter.

CEO Rodrigo Barbosa said Aura Minerals remained on track to meet its full-year targets, with further growth expected in Q4. The company also noted that work at its Era Dorada project remained on time and on budget, with overall physical progress at 13.1%. Aura Minerals plans to keep advancing its mine upgrades and the MSG turnaround as it works to lift output in the final quarter.

AUGO Stock Soars Today

Aura Minerals stock was up 11.5% on Friday, extending an 87.51% rally year-to-date. The shares have also climbed 123.37% higher over the past 12 months.

Even with today's news, trading of AUGO stock was limited. Some 528,000 shares changed hands today, compared to a three-month average daily trading volume of about 986,000 shares.

Turning to Wall Street, the analysts' consensus rating for Aura Minerals is Strong Buy, based on three Buy and one Sell ratings over the past three months. With that comes an average AUGO stock price target of $105.23, representing a potential 14.47% upside for the shares. (See AUGO Stock Forecast)

data.title: AST SpaceMobile CEO Touts Spectrum 'No One Can Match' as ASTS Stock Sinks 15% on SpaceX Threat
data.description:
Shares in AST SpaceMobile (ASTS), the satellite-based cellular network builder, plunged by 15% to about $49 on Friday afternoon, extending the previous day's 6.13% fall. This followed an industry-wide sell-off after aerospace and rocket giant SpaceX (SPCX) confirmed it had agreed to buy 800 MHz of low-band spectrum from private investment firm Grain Management. Reports estimate the deal at $8 billion, with the move seen as a potential threat to traditional network providers. Reacting, Abel Avellan, AST's chair and CEO, boasted in an X post that the company can deploy "critical low-band and mid-band spectrum that no one can match!"

Why ASTS Stock Is Plunging on SpaceX's $8B Spectrum Push

For context, low-band spectrum is radio frequency "lanes" that can travel farther and penetrate buildings. Mid-band spectrum, meanwhile, travels far less but carries more data.

Investors appear to think acquiring the spectrum portfolio could help SpaceX's Starlink compete directly with the country's largest carriers, AT&T (T), Verizon (VZ), and T-Mobile U.S. (TMUS) in metropolitan areas. This could be achieved through a hybrid terrestrial infrastructure.

Promotion

ASTX: an alternative to margin or options on ASTS

In addition, as Starlink already offers a well-established satellite network targeting rural areas, investors also seem to think this ground-and-space expansion could give SpaceX a decisive advantage over AST. Notably, AST relies on partnerships with those same legacy carriers.

AST Defends Advantage Amid SpaceX Threat

In the X post, Avellan noted that its U.S. mobile carrier partners have about 1,000 MHz of low- and mid-band spectrum that his company's satellite network can use. He also pointed to the company's own portfolio of 45 MHz of L-band spectrum.

This spectrum also travels relatively far. It can also handle obstacles such as weather, trees, and buildings better than higher-frequency bands.

"With our current satellites in orbit and in build, our United States partners will access critical low-band and mid-band spectrum that no one can match!" Avellan wrote.

He continued, "When combined with the mobile network operators' extensive spectrum assets, and in combination with AST SpaceMobile-controlled 45 MHz of L-band spectrum, users will see peak data rates of nearly 200 Mbps from the largest-ever satellites in low Earth orbit."

Is AST SpaceMobile Stock a Good Buy or Sell?

On Wall Street, AST SpaceMobile's shares remain a Moderate Buy based on analysts' consensus ratings. This breaks down into five Buys and six Holds issued by 11 analysts over the past three months.

However, the average ASTS price target of $86.42 suggests about 77% upside ahead (see ASTS stock forecast here).

data.title: Shareholders Sue Innventure Over DarkNX Data Center Partnership Claims
data.description:
A class action lawsuit was filed against tech group Innventure (INV) on August 28, 2026. Plaintiffs in the federal securities lawsuit allege that they acquired Innventure stock at artificially inflated prices between November 17, 2025 and August 13, 2026, known as the Class Period. They are now seeking compensation for financial losses incurred upon public revelation of the company's alleged misconduct during that time. To learn whether you may be eligible for a recovery under this securities lawsuit, click here.

What Does INV Do?

Innventure is an industrial technology commercialization company. The company primarily operates through Accelsius Holdings LLC, a subsidiary focused on developing and commercializing two-phase, direct-to-chip liquid cooling solutions for data centers and high-performance computing environments, referred to as NeuCool technology.

Why are Shareholders Suing INV?

The Innventure shareholder lawsuit centers on Accelsius, the company's subsidiary focused on NeuCool liquid cooling technology for AI data centers and high-performance computing environments. According to the complaint, Innventure began the class period by announcing that DarkNX would deploy Accelsius' NeuCool technology across a new 300MW AI data center campus in Ontario, Canada, describing the project as expected to be the largest two-phase, direct-to-chip deployment to date.

data.title: Delta Air Lines Stock (DAL) Loses Altitude After Poor Earnings and Guidance Cut
data.description:
The stock of Delta Air Line (DAL) was down as much as 4% on Oct. 9 after the carrier reported poor financial results and lowered its forward guidance. DAL stock is losing altitude after the Atlanta, Georgia-based carrier posted its first time top and bottom-line misses in two years, shaking investor confidence in the airline's outlook.

Delta reported earnings per share of $1.72, which was below the $1.75 forecast among analysts. Revenue in the July through September period amounted to $17.59 billion, which fell short of the $17.67 billion expected on Wall Street. Delta's net income of $756 million was down 47% from $1.42 billion a year earlier.

data.title: Tesla China-Made EV Sales Rise for 11th Straight Month
data.description:
Electric vehicle maker Tesla (TSLA) sold 95,366 China-made Model 3 and Model Y vehicles in September, which was an increase of 5% from 90,812 a year earlier. This was its 11th consecutive month of annual growth and an improvement from August's 3.6% increase. Importantly, the figures from the China Passenger Car Association include vehicles sold in China and exported to other markets. At the same time, stronger overseas demand helped Tesla maintain its sales momentum despite weaker demand from Chinese buyers.

In fact, Tesla shipped 30,529 vehicles overseas, an increase of 58% from last year. Meanwhile, domestic sales fell by 9% to 64,837 vehicles.

Europe helped support that export growth as Tesla continued recovering from two years of declining sales in the region. September registrations in France grew by 61.9% from last year, while Portugal recorded a 128.3% increase. Sweden also posted growth of 38.4%.

The improvement helped Tesla's Shanghai-made vehicle sales grow by 13.7% during the third quarter. However, the company's global deliveries fell by 2.1% from last year's record quarter, even though its 486,532 deliveries exceeded Wall Street expectations of approximately 461,000.

Tesla Is Offering Discounts as Competition in China Remains Intense

Despite the stronger exports, Tesla is still having difficulty growing its domestic business. That has led the company to offer discounts to attract more Chinese buyers. Through the end of October, Tesla is offering final-payment discounts of 7,000 yuan, or about $1,044, on selected Model Y variants. Customers purchasing any Model 3 variant can also receive a 5,000-yuan discount.

Those incentives could help Tesla generate additional sales, although lower prices may put pressure on its profit margins.

Meanwhile, the company's global delivery figures have improved this year. Tesla delivered 1.32 million vehicles during the first nine months of 2026, an increase of 8.8% from the same period last year. That puts Tesla in a position to return to annual delivery growth after two consecutive years of declines.

Tesla is scheduled to report its third-quarter financial results on October 21, when investors will get another look at its automotive profitability.

data.title: Nvidia Stock (NVDA) Struggles After OpenAI Revenue Disclosure
data.description:
The stock of chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA) is down 1% a day after artificial intelligence (AI) startup OpenAI disclosed revised revenue figures that have rattled investors. The decline on Oct. 9 comes after NVDA stock dropped 3% in the previous trading session on news of OpenAI's sales.

Stocks of companies tied to the artificial intelligence (A.I.) buildout fell after OpenAI announced a revised revenue figure that fell short of Wall Street's expectations. data.title: Top Five Biggest Video Game Stock Stories This Week, 10/9/26
data.description:
The video game industry saw big announcements this week. Console sales fell as prices rose, while Xbox hinted at new hardware plans. Nintendo also set up a busy holiday season, and Sony explored new ways to engage stream viewers. Meanwhile, Cyberpunk 2077 is heading to the big screen.

1. Game Hardware Sales Hit a 13-Year Low

A global shortage of memory and storage parts has pushed console prices higher. Sony (SONY), Microsoft (MSFT), and Nintendo (NTDOY) have all raised prices. New data from Circana shows that U.S. game hardware sales fell 15% year over year in August. Sales hit their lowest level since 2013, as higher prices may be keeping some buyers away from new systems.

2. Xbox Hints at a New Handheld

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has fueled talk of a new Xbox handheld. The device may be part of the next-gen hardware line known as Project Helix. This also isn't the first time reports of an Xbox handheld have spread online. The hints come as Sony faces questions about its own plans for a handheld system. Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden has warned that Sony has often struggled to market a home console and a handheld at the same time.

3. Nintendo Plans a Big Zelda Holiday Push

Nintendo is lining up four major releases in a tight 14-day span to mark the Zelda series' 40th anniversary. The plan is to release new games and hardware during the holiday season. The schedule is said to end with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, which is set to launch worldwide on November 5, 2026.

4. Sony Patent Lets Stream Viewers Join the Game

Sony has filed a patent for tech that could let viewers affect a streamer's gameplay. The system could give viewers control of a shared on-screen cursor or let them send signals based on their reactions. These tools could help fans guide a player—or make the game harder. The idea could add a new layer of audience input to live game streams.

5. Cyberpunk 2077 Is Getting a Live-Action Film

CD Projekt Red (OTGLF) is teaming up with Skydance (SKYD)'s Paramount Pictures to co-produce a live-action Cyberpunk 2077 film. The project will bring the game world to the big screen. It adds to the growing link between video games and film, as game-based stories reach fans across more forms of media.
